claims.statement: Persephone is a Greek goddess of agriculture and vegetation and wife of Hades.
claims.statement_id: Persephone adalah dewi pertanian dan tumbuhan Yunani serta istri Hades.
claims.quote: Persephone (aka Kore) was the Greek goddess of agriculture and vegetation, especially grain, and the wife of Hades, the ruler of the Underworld.

claims.statement: Kore means daughter and maiden.
claims.statement_id: Nama Kore berarti anak perempuan dan gadis.
claims.quote: In this guise she is most often referred to as Kore, signifying both 'daughter' and 'maiden'.

claims.statement: As Hades's wife, Persephone is queen of the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai istri Hades, Persephone adalah ratu dunia bawah.
claims.quote: In Greek mythology, the goddess, as wife of Hades, is the Queen of the Underworld and takes her other name, Persephone.

claims.statement: Hades abducted Persephone while she picked flowers and took her to the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Hades menculik Persephone saat ia memetik bunga dan membawanya ke dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Hades abducted Persephone while she was picking flowers with her companions in a meadow and carried her off to the Underworld

claims.statement: Demeter's grief caused crop failure, prompting Zeus to demand Persephone's return.
claims.statement_id: Kesedihan Demeter menyebabkan gagal panen sehingga Zeus meminta Hades mengembalikan Persephone.
claims.quote: There the wrath of the distressed mother caused a complete failure of the crops, prompting Zeus to order his brother Hades to return the girl.

claims.statement: Pomegranate seeds obliged Persephone to spend part of the year below and the rest with Demeter.
claims.statement_id: Karena biji delima, Persephone harus menghabiskan sebagian tahun di dunia bawah dan sisanya bersama Demeter.
claims.quote: He cunningly tricked Persephone into eating some pomegranate seeds before leaving, thus condemning her to spend part of the year in the Underworld as his wife and the rest among the living with Demeter

claims.statement: The story may symbolize seasonal change and life's cycle.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini dapat melambangkan pergantian musim dan daur kehidupan.
claims.quote: The story of Demeter, Hades and Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons and the perennial change from life to death, to life once more

claims.statement: Persephone was linked to the Eleusinian Mysteries and Thesmophoria.
claims.statement_id: Persephone terkait dengan Misteri Eleusis dan perayaan Thesmophoria.
claims.quote: Persephone was an important element of the Eleusinian Mysteries and the Thesmophoria festival and so the goddess was worshipped throughout the Greek world.

claims.statement: The Eleusinian relief depicts Persephone on the right as Demeter's daughter.
claims.statement_id: Relief Eleusis menggambarkan Persephone di sisi kanan sebagai putri Demeter.
claims.quote: At the right is Persephone, her daughter and the wife of Hades, the god of the underworld.

claims.statement: Hades, god of the Underworld, fell in love with the beautiful Persephone when he saw her picking flowers in a meadow, then carried her off in his chariot to the dark Underworld.
claims.statement_id: Hades, dewa dunia bawah, jatuh cinta pada Persephone yang cantik ketika melihatnya memetik bunga di padang rumput, lalu membawanya dengan kereta ke dunia bawah yang gelap.
claims.quote: Hades, god of the Underworld, fell in love with beautiful Persephone when he saw her picking flowers one day in a meadow. The god then carried her off in his chariot to live with him in the dark Underworld.

claims.statement: In some accounts Zeus had consented to the abduction, and the location is traditionally placed in either Sicily (famed for its fertility) or Asia.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi Zeus menyetujui penculikan itu, dan lokasinya secara tradisional ditempatkan di Sisilia (termasyhur kesuburannya) atau Asia.
claims.quote: In some accounts, Zeus had given his consent to the abduction, the location of the crime being traditionally placed in either Sicily (famed for its fertility) or Asia.

claims.statement: Demeter searched the earth for her lost daughter; though Helios (or Hermes) told her her daughter's fate, she kept wandering until she arrived at Eleusis.
claims.statement_id: Demeter mencari putrinya ke seluruh bumi; meski Helios (atau Hermes) memberitahunya nasib putrinya, ia terus berkelana hingga tiba di Eleusis.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, Demeter searched the earth for her lost divine daughter and though Helios (or Hermes) told her of her daughter's fate, she, nevertheless, continued her wanderings until she finally arrived at Eleusis.

claims.statement: Once the temple was finished, Demeter withdrew into it and created a great drought to convince the other gods to release Persephone; as the drought claimed more victims, Zeus sent Hermes to persuade Hades to release her.
claims.statement_id: Setelah kuil selesai, Demeter menarik diri dan tinggal di dalamnya sambil menciptakan kekeringan besar agar dewa-dewa lain melepaskan Persephone; ketika korban kekeringan bertambah, Zeus mengutus Hermes membujuk Hades.
claims.quote: Once the temple was completed, Demeter withdrew from the world and lived inside it; at the same time, she created a great drought to convince the other gods to release Persephone from Hades. As the drought claimed ever more victims, Zeus finally sent Hermes to persuade Hades to release his ill-gotten bride.

claims.statement: Before giving her up, the wily Hades put a pomegranate kernel in her mouth, knowing its divine taste would compel her to return to him.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum melepasnya, Hades yang licik menaruh sebutir biji delima di mulut Persephone karena tahu rasa ilahinya akan memaksanya kembali.
claims.quote: Before giving her up though, the wily Hades put a pomegranate kernel in the girl's mouth, knowing its divine taste would compel her to return to him.

claims.statement: As a compromise, it was decided Persephone would be released but must return to Hades for one-third of the year (or one-half in other accounts).
claims.statement_id: Sebagai kompromi, diputuskan Persephone dilepas tetapi harus kembali kepada Hades selama sepertiga tahun (atau separuh tahun dalam versi lain).
claims.quote: Finally, as a compromise, it was decided that Persephone would be released but that she would have to return to Hades for one-third of the year (or in other accounts one-half).

claims.statement: Another interpretation is that the myth represents the Greeks storing their grain underground for part of the year to protect it from summer heat.
claims.statement_id: Tafsiran lain: mitos itu mungkin menggambarkan saat orang Yunani menyimpan gandum di bawah tanah selama sebagian tahun untuk melindunginya dari panas musim panas.
claims.quote: Another interpretation of the Persephone myth may be that it represents when the Greeks stored their grain underground for part of the year in order to protect it from summer heat.

claims.statement: Persephone's cult was especially strong in Sicily and southern Italy; besides the Eleusinian Mysteries at Eleusis there were sanctuaries across the Greek world, notably at Locri Epizephyrii, Mantinea, Megalopolis and Sparta.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Persephone dalam agama Yunani sangat kuat di Sisilia dan Italia selatan; selain Misteri Eleusis di Eleusis, ada tempat suci untuknya di seluruh dunia Yunani, terutama di Locri Epizephyrii, Mantinea, Megalopolis, dan Sparta.
claims.quote: The cult of Persephone in the Greek religion was especially strong in Sicily and southern Italy, and besides the Eleusinian Mysteries at Eleusis there were sanctuaries to the goddess across the Greek world, most notably at Locri Epizephyrii, Mantinea, Megalopolis, and Sparta.

claims.statement: The Thesmophoria was a Greek-wide celebration of the goddess and her mother, exclusive to women and held annually before sowing, when sacrifices were made and putrefied pig remains were mixed with the seeds.
claims.statement_id: Thesmophoria adalah perayaan seluruh Yunani untuk sang dewi dan ibunya; khusus perempuan, diadakan tiap tahun sebelum masa menabur, dengan kurban dan sisa babi yang membusuk dicampur ke benih.
claims.quote: The Thesmophoria was a Greek-wide celebration of the goddess and her mother. Exclusive to women, it was held annually before the sowing period when sacrifices were made and putrefied pig's remains were mixed with the seeds.

claims.statement: As Queen of the Underworld, Persephone was often appealed to in curse tablets and on inscribed gold leaves buried with dead followers of Orphism.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai Ratu Dunia Bawah, Persephone sering dimohon dalam tablet kutukan dan pada lembaran emas bertulis yang dikubur bersama pengikut Orfisme yang meninggal.
claims.quote: Persephone, in her guise as Queen of the Underworld, was often appealed to in curse tablets and on the inscribed gold leaves buried with the dead followers of Orphism which gave instructions on how to conduct themselves in the after-life.

claims.statement: In that guise she was seen as a protectress in the after-life, although Hesiod repeatedly calls her "dread Persephone" in his Theogony.
claims.statement_id: Dalam peran itu ia dipandang sebagai pelindung di alam baka, meski Hesiodos berulang kali menyebutnya "Persephone yang menakutkan" dalam Theogony.
claims.quote: In this guise, she was seen as a protectress in the after-life, although Hesiod repeatedly describes her as 'dread Persephone' in his Theogony.

claims.statement: Persephone rarely appears in art before the 6th century BCE, then is usually shown with Demeter; both often wear crowns and hold a torch, sceptre or stalks of grain.
claims.statement_id: Persephone jarang muncul dalam seni sebelum abad ke-6 SM, dan kemudian biasanya ditampilkan bersama Demeter; keduanya sering bermahkota dan memegang obor, tongkat kerajaan, atau tangkai gandum.
claims.quote: Persephone rarely appears in art before the 6th century BCE, and then she is usually shown with Demeter; often both wear crowns and hold a torch, sceptre, or stalks of grain.

claims.statement: In various other myths Persephone is the mother of Dionysos (by Zeus, who is also her father), though Semele is the more usual candidate, and she squabbles with Aphrodite over Adonis, the two agreeing to share the lover in turns.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa mitos lain Persephone ibu Dionysos (dengan Zeus, yang juga ayahnya), meski Semele kandidat yang lebih lazim, dan ia bersaing dengan Aphrodite memperebutkan Adonis hingga keduanya sepakat berbagi sang kekasih bergiliran.
claims.quote: In various other myths, Persephone is the mother of Dionysos (with Zeus, who is also her father) - although Semele is the more usual candidate - and squabbles with Aphrodite for the attentions of devilishly handsome Adonis, the two settling to share the famous lover in split shifts.

claims.statement: A famous relief slab from Eleusis shows Demeter and Persephone (holding a torch) on either side of Triptolemos; it dates to the 5th century BCE.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah lempeng relief terkenal dari Eleusis menampilkan Demeter dan Persephone (memegang obor) di kedua sisi Triptolemos; berasal dari abad ke-5 SM.
claims.quote: A famous relief slab from Eleusis depicts Demeter and Persephone (holding a torch) either side of Triptolemos; it dates to the 5th century BCE.

claims.statement: In other versions Persephone could have been released had she eaten nothing in the underworld, but at the last moment Hades gave her a pomegranate seed.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain Persephone bisa dibebaskan seandainya ia tidak makan apa pun di dunia bawah, tetapi pada detik terakhir Hades memberinya sebutir biji delima.
claims.quote: In other versions of the myth, Persephone could have been released if she had not eaten anything in the underworld during her captivity, but at the last moment, Hades gave her a pomegranate seed.

claims.statement: In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter the girl was amazed and reached out with both hands for the lovely flower; then the earth yawned in the plain of Nysa and the lord, Host of Many, sprang out with his immortal horses.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Himne Homerik untuk Demeter, gadis itu takjub dan mengulurkan kedua tangan untuk mengambil bunga itu; lalu bumi menganga di dataran Nysa dan Sang Tuan Banyak Tamu melompat keluar dengan kuda-kuda abadinya.
claims.quote: and the girl was amazed and reached out with both hands to take the lovely toy; but the wide-pathed earth yawned there in the plain of Nysa, and the lord, Host of Many, with his immortal horses sprang out upon her

claims.statement: The narcissus was made to grow by Earth at the will of Zeus and to please the Host of Many, as a snare for the bloom-like girl.
claims.statement_id: Bunga narsis itu ditumbuhkan Bumi atas kehendak Zeus dan untuk menyenangkan Sang Tuan Banyak Tamu, sebagai jerat bagi gadis yang segar bagai bunga.
claims.quote: which Earth made to grow at the will of Zeus and to please the Host of Many, to be a snare for the bloom-like girl

claims.statement: Only tender-hearted Hecate, daughter of Persaeus, heard the girl from her cave, and the lord Helios, Hyperion's bright son.
claims.statement_id: Hanya Hecate yang berhati lembut, putri Persaeus, mendengar teriakan gadis itu dari guanya, begitu pula tuan Helios, putra Hyperion yang cemerlang.
claims.quote: only tender-hearted Hecate, bright-coiffed, the daughter of Persaeus, heard the girl from her cave, and the lord Helios, Hyperion's bright son

claims.statement: In the Homeric Hymn Hades tells Persephone that while she is there she shall rule all that lives and moves and have the greatest rights among the gods; those who defraud her and do not appease her power with offerings shall be punished for evermore.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik, Hades berkata kepada Persephone bahwa selama di sana ia akan memerintah semua yang hidup dan bergerak dan memiliki hak terbesar di antara para dewa; mereka yang menipunya dan tidak menenangkan kuasanya dengan persembahan akan dihukum selamanya.
claims.quote: And while you are here, you shall rule all that lives and moves and shall have the greatest rights among the deathless gods: those who defraud you and do not appease your power with offerings, reverently performing rites and paying fit gifts, shall be punished for evermore.

claims.statement: Hades secretly gave her sweet pomegranate seed to eat, taking care that she might not remain continually with Demeter.
claims.statement_id: Hades diam-diam memberinya biji delima manis untuk dimakan agar ia tidak terus-menerus tinggal bersama Demeter.
claims.quote: But he on his part secretly gave her sweet pomegranate seed to eat, taking care for himself that she might not remain continually with grave, dark-robed Demeter.

claims.statement: Demeter says that if Persephone has tasted food she must go back beneath the earth to dwell a third part of the seasons every year, and for the other two parts be with her and the other gods.
claims.statement_id: Demeter berkata: jika Persephone telah mencicipi makanan, ia harus kembali ke bawah bumi dan tinggal di sana sepertiga musim setiap tahun, sedangkan dua bagian lainnya ia bersama Demeter dan para dewa.
claims.quote: if you have tasted food, you must go back again beneath the secret places of the earth, there to dwell a third part of the seasons every year: yet for the two parts you shall be with me and the other deathless gods.

claims.statement: When the earth blooms with the fragrant flowers of spring, Persephone shall come up once more from the realm of darkness to be a wonder for gods and mortals.
claims.statement_id: Ketika bumi mekar dengan bunga-bunga musim semi yang harum, Persephone akan naik lagi dari alam gelap menjadi keajaiban bagi dewa dan manusia.
claims.quote: But when the earth shall bloom with the fragrant flowers of spring in every kind, then from the realm of darkness and gloom thou shalt come up once more to be a wonder for gods and mortal men.

claims.statement: From that time Hecate was minister and companion to Persephone.
claims.statement_id: Sejak saat itu Hecate menjadi pelayan dan pendamping Persephone.
claims.quote: from that time the lady Hecate was minister and companion to Persephone.

claims.statement: Persephone (Περσεφόνη in Ancient Greek) is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter; she became queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage.
claims.statement_id: Persephone (Περσεφόνη dalam bahasa Yunani Kuno) adalah putri Zeus dan Demeter; ia menjadi ratu dunia bawah setelah diculik pamannya, Hades, raja dunia bawah, yang kemudian menikahinya.
claims.quote: Ancient Greek: Περσεφόνη ) is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter. She became the queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, the king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage.

claims.statement: The myth of her abduction, sojourn in the underworld and cyclical return to the surface represents her functions as embodiment of spring and personification of vegetation, especially grain crops.
claims.statement_id: Mitos penculikan, masa tinggalnya di dunia bawah, dan kembalinya yang berulang ke permukaan mewakili fungsinya sebagai perwujudan musim semi dan personifikasi tumbuhan, terutama tanaman biji-bijian.
claims.quote: The myth of her abduction, her sojourn in the underworld, and her cyclical return to the surface represents her functions as the embodiment of spring and the personification of vegetation, especially grain crops

claims.statement: In Classical Greek art Persephone is invariably robed, often carrying a sheaf of grain; she may appear as a mystical divinity with a sceptre and a little box, but was mostly shown being carried off by Hades.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni Yunani Klasik, Persephone selalu digambarkan berjubah, sering membawa seikat gandum; ia dapat tampil sebagai dewi mistik dengan tongkat dan kotak kecil, tetapi paling sering ditampilkan saat dibawa pergi Hades.
claims.quote: In Classical Greek art, Persephone is invariably portrayed robed, often carrying a sheaf of grain. She may appear as a mystical divinity with a sceptre and a little box, but she was mostly represented in the process of being carried off by Hades.

claims.statement: Persephone as a vegetation goddess and her mother Demeter were the central figures of the Eleusinian Mysteries, which promised initiates a happy afterlife.
claims.statement_id: Persephone sebagai dewi tumbuhan dan ibunya, Demeter, adalah tokoh sentral Misteri Eleusis yang menjanjikan akhirat bahagia bagi para penganutnya.
claims.quote: Persephone, as a vegetation goddess, and her mother Demeter were the central figures of the Eleusinian Mysteries, which promised the initiated a happy afterlife.

claims.statement: In the region of the city of Epizephyrian Locris, in modern Calabria (southern Italy), she is a goddess of marriage and childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Di wilayah kota Locris Epizephyria, di Calabria modern (Italia selatan), ia adalah dewi pernikahan dan kelahiran.
claims.quote: She is a goddess of marriage and childbirth in the region of the city of Epizephyrian Locris, in modern Calabria (southern Italy).

claims.statement: In Latin her name is rendered Proserpina; the Romans identified her as Libera, an Italic goddess conflated with Proserpina.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Latin namanya menjadi Proserpina; orang Romawi mengidentifikasinya sebagai Libera, dewi Italik yang dipadukan dengan Proserpina.
claims.quote: In Latin, her name is rendered Proserpina. She was identified by the Romans as Libera, an Italic goddess who was conflated with Proserpina.

claims.statement: The etymology of "Persephone" is obscure; a popular folk etymology links it to pherein phonon, "to bring (or cause) death".
claims.statement_id: Asal kata "Persephone" tidak jelas; etimologi rakyat yang populer mengaitkannya dengan pherein phonon, "membawa (atau menyebabkan) kematian".
claims.quote: The etymology of the word "Persephone" is obscure. ... pherein phonon, "to bring (or cause) death".

claims.statement: Günther Zuntz considers "Persephone" and "Kore" distinct deities ("no farmer prayed for corn to Persephone; no mourner thought of the dead as being with Kore"), but ancient Greek writers were not as consistent as he claims.
claims.statement_id: Günther Zuntz menganggap "Persephone" dan "Kore" dewi yang berbeda ("tak ada petani memohon gandum kepada Persephone; tak ada orang berduka membayangkan yang mati bersama Kore"), tetapi para penulis Yunani kuno tidak sekonsisten klaimnya.
claims.quote: Günther Zuntz considers "Persephone" and "Kore" as distinct deities and writes that "no farmer prayed for corn to Persephone; no mourner thought of the dead as being with Kore." Ancient Greek writers were, however, not as consistent as Zuntz claims.

claims.statement: Myths similar to Persephone's descent and return also appear in the cults of male gods, including Attis, Adonis and Osiris, and in Minoan Crete.
claims.statement_id: Mitos serupa turunnya Persephone dan kembalinya ke bumi juga muncul dalam kultus dewa-dewa laki-laki, termasuk Attis, Adonis, dan Osiris, serta di Kreta Minoa.
claims.quote: Myths similar to Persephone's descent and return to earth also appear in the cults of male gods, including Attis, Adonis, and Osiris, and in Minoan Crete.

claims.statement: Persephone's epithets reveal her double function as chthonic and vegetation goddess.
claims.statement_id: Julukan Persephone menunjukkan fungsi gandanya sebagai dewi kekuatan bawah tanah (khthonik) dan dewi tumbuhan.
claims.quote: The epithets of Persephone reveal her double function as chthonic and vegetation goddess.

claims.statement: According to a hypothesis by Rudolf Wachter, the combined sense of the name would be "she who beats the ears of corn", i.e. a "thresher of grain".
claims.statement_id: Menurut hipotesis Rudolf Wachter, makna gabungan namanya adalah "ia yang memukul bulir gandum", yaitu "perontok gandum".
claims.quote: According to a recent hypothesis advanced by Rudolf Wachter ... The combined sense would therefore be "she who beats the ears of corn", i.e., a "thresher of grain"

claims.statement: In cult she was often referred to as Kore.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kultus ia sering disebut Kore.
claims.quote: In cult, she was often referred to as Kore

claims.statement: Asclepius is the Greek god of medicine and was credited with prophecy.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius adalah dewa pengobatan Yunani yang juga dikaitkan dengan ramalan.
claims.quote: Asclepius was the ancient Greek god of medicine, and he was also credited with powers of prophecy.

claims.statement: Asclepius was a son of Apollo and Koronis in one account.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius adalah putra Apollo dan Koronis menurut salah satu kisah.
claims.quote: In Greek mythology, Asclepius (or Asklepios) was a demigod hero as he was the son of divine Apollo, and his mother was the mortal Koronis from Thessaly.

claims.statement: The centaur Chiron taught Asclepius.
claims.statement_id: Centaur Chiron mengajar Asclepius.
claims.quote: Asclepius was also tutored by Cheiron, the wise centaur who lived on Mt. Pelion.

claims.statement: Zeus killed Asclepius with a thunderbolt.
claims.statement_id: Zeus membunuh Asclepius dengan petir.
claims.quote: Asclepius met a tragic end when he was killed by a thunderbolt thrown by Zeus.

claims.statement: Asclepius was deified after his death.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius didewakan setelah kematiannya.
claims.quote: Asclepius himself was deified following his death, and in some local myths, he also became the constellation Ophiuchus.

claims.statement: Asclepius was especially worshipped at Epidaurus.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius terutama dipuja di tempat suci Epidaurus.
claims.quote: The god was particularly worshipped at the sanctuary of Epidaurus (founded in the 6th century BCE), known as the Asklepieion

claims.statement: At Epidaurus, patients slept awaiting dreams offering cures from the god.
claims.statement_id: Di Epidaurus, pasien tidur menunggu mimpi tentang pengobatan dari dewa.
claims.quote: At Epidaurus, there was also the columned Abato or Enkoimeterion in which patients, after having gone through several purification rituals, slept overnight and awaited dreams where the god would appear and offer cures and remedies.

claims.statement: Asclepius is depicted bearded with a snake-entwined staff, a modern medical symbol.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius digambarkan berjanggut dengan tongkat berlilit ular, lambang pengobatan modern.
claims.quote: Almost always, the god has a full beard, wears a simple himation robe, and holds a staff (the bakteria) with a sacred snake coiled around it, which has become the modern symbol of medicine.

claims.statement: His cult was brought to Rome in snake form and given a temple on Tiber Island.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Asclepius dibawa ke Roma dalam wujud ular dan diberi kuil di Pulau Tiber.
claims.quote: The god was fetched from Epidaurus in the form of a snake and a temple assigned him on the island in the Tiber

claims.statement: Epidaurus was an important healing centre in Greek and Roman times.
claims.statement_id: Epidaurus adalah pusat penyembuhan penting bagi Yunani dan Romawi kuno.
claims.quote: The god had several sanctuaries across Greece; the most famous was at Epidaurus which became an important centre of healing in both ancient Greek and Roman times

claims.statement: Asklepios was the god of medicine and also the patron god and reputed ancestor of the Asklepiades, the ancient guild of doctors.
claims.statement_id: Asklepios adalah dewa pengobatan, sekaligus dewa pelindung dan leluhur yang dipercaya dari Asklepiades, serikat dokter kuno.
claims.quote: ASKLEPIOS (Asclepius) was the god of medicine. He was also the patron god, and reputed ancestor, of the Asklepiades (Asclepiades), the ancient guild of doctors.

claims.statement: His mother died in labour and when she was laid on the pyre Apollo cut the unborn child from her womb; from this Asklepios received his name, which means "to cut open".
claims.statement_id: Ibunya meninggal saat bersalin dan ketika jenazahnya diletakkan di pembakaran, Apollo membedah rahimnya untuk mengambil bayi itu; dari sini Asklepios menerima namanya yang berarti "membelah".
claims.quote: His mother died in labour and when she was laid out on the pyre, Apollon cut the unborn child from her womb. From this Asklepios received his name which means "to cut open."

claims.statement: He grew so skilled that he could restore the dead to life; this was a crime against the natural order, so Zeus destroyed him with a thunderbolt.
claims.statement_id: Ia begitu terampil sehingga mampu menghidupkan orang mati; ini kejahatan terhadap tatanan alam sehingga Zeus menghancurkannya dengan petir.
claims.quote: He grew so skilled in the craft that he was able to restore the dead to life. This was a crime against the natural order and so Zeus destroyed him with a thunderbolt.

claims.statement: After his death Asklepios was placed among the stars as the constellation Ophiochus ("the Serpent Holder").
claims.statement_id: Setelah kematiannya Asklepios ditempatkan di antara bintang sebagai rasi Ophiochus ("Pemegang Ular").
claims.quote: After his death Asklepios was placed amongst the stars as the constellation Ophiochus ("the Serpent Holder").

claims.statement: According to Apollodorus' summary, he received from Athena the blood from the Gorgon's veins: the left side he used to destroy people, the right to preserve them, which is how he could revive the dead.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Apollodorus, ia menerima dari Athena darah dari pembuluh Gorgon: bagian sisi kiri dipakai untuk membinasakan orang, sisi kanan untuk menyelamatkan, sehingga ia dapat menghidupkan kembali orang yang mati.
claims.quote: he had received from Athena the blood that had coursed though the Gorgon's veins, the left-side portion of which he used to destroy people, but that on the right he used for their preservation, which is how he could revive those who had died.

claims.statement: Zeus was afraid men might learn medicine from Asklepios and help each other, so he struck him with a thunderbolt; this angered Apollo, who slew the Cyclopes who designed the thunderbolt for Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Zeus takut manusia akan belajar ilmu pengobatan dari Asklepios dan saling menolong, maka ia menyambarnya dengan petir; Apollo yang murka membunuh para Kiklops yang merancang petir itu bagi Zeus.
claims.quote: Zeus was afraid that men might learn the art of medicine from Asklepios and help each other out, so he hit him with a thunderbolt. This angered Apollon, who slew the Kyklopes (Cyclopes), for they designed the thunderbolt for Zeus.

claims.statement: These temples were not only places of worship but were frequented by great numbers of sick persons and may therefore be compared to modern hospitals.
claims.statement_id: Kuil-kuil itu bukan hanya tempat ibadah tetapi juga didatangi banyak orang sakit sehingga dapat dibandingkan dengan rumah sakit modern.
claims.quote: These temples were not only places of worship, but were frequented by great numbers of sick persons, and may therefore be compared to modern hospitals.

claims.statement: The principal seat of his worship in Greece was Epidaurus, where his temple was surrounded by an extensive grove within which no one was allowed to die and no woman to give birth.
claims.statement_id: Pusat utama pemujaannya di Yunani adalah Epidaurus, dengan kuil yang dikelilingi hutan luas; di dalamnya tak seorang pun boleh meninggal dan tak seorang perempuan pun boleh melahirkan.
claims.quote: The principal seat of his worship in Greece was Epidaurus, where he had a temple surrounded with an extensive grove, within which no one was allowed to die, and no woman to give birth to a child.

claims.statement: Serpents were connected with the worship of Aesculapius everywhere, probably as a symbol of prudence and renovation, and were believed able to discover herbs of wondrous powers.
claims.statement_id: Ular terkait dengan pemujaan Aesculapius di mana-mana, mungkin karena melambangkan kebijaksanaan dan pembaruan serta dipercaya mampu menemukan ramuan berkhasiat ajaib.
claims.quote: Serpents were everywhere connected with the worship of Aesculapius, probably because they were a symbol of prudence and renovation, and were believed to have the power of discovering herbs of wondrous powers

claims.statement: At Epidaurus he was shown seated on a throne, holding a staff in one hand and resting the other on the head of a dragon (serpent), with a dog by his side.
claims.statement_id: Di Epidaurus ia digambarkan duduk di singgasana, satu tangan memegang tongkat dan tangan lain bertumpu pada kepala naga (ular), dengan seekor anjing di sisinya.
claims.quote: He was seated on a throne, holding in one hand a staff, and with the other resting upon the head of a dragon (serpent), and by his side lay a dog.

claims.statement: Medical knowledge was regarded as a sacred secret transmitted from father to son in the families of the Asclepiadae.
claims.statement_id: Pengetahuan pengobatan dianggap rahasia suci yang diwariskan dari ayah ke anak dalam keluarga Asclepiadae.
claims.quote: The knowledge of medicine was regarded as a sacred secret, which was transmitted from father to son in the families of the Asclepiadae

claims.statement: In the Homeric poems Aesculapius does not appear to be considered a divinity, but merely a human being.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi-puisi Homeros, Aesculapius tampaknya tidak dianggap dewa, melainkan sekadar manusia.
claims.quote: In the Homeric poems Aesculapius does not appear to be considered as a divinity, but merely as a human being

claims.statement: Asklepios was depicted as a kindly, bearded man holding a serpent-entwined staff.
claims.statement_id: Asklepios digambarkan sebagai lelaki ramah berjanggut yang memegang tongkat berlilit ular.
claims.quote: Asklepios was depicted as a kindly, bearded man holding a serpent-entwined staff.

claims.statement: Homeric Hymn XVI sings of Asclepius, son of Apollo and healer of sicknesses.
claims.statement_id: Himne Homerik XVI menyanyikan Asclepius, putra Apollo dan penyembuh penyakit.
claims.quote: I begin to sing of Asclepius, son of Apollo and healer of sicknesses.

claims.statement: According to the Hymn, Coronis, daughter of King Phlegyas, bore him in the Dotian plain, a great joy to men and a soother of cruel pangs.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Himne itu, Koronis, putri Raja Phlegyas, melahirkannya di dataran Dotion; ia sukacita besar bagi manusia dan penenang rasa sakit yang kejam.
claims.quote: In the Dotian plain fair Coronis, daughter of King Phlegyas, bare him, a great joy to men, a soother of cruel pangs.

claims.statement: All who were healed offered sacrifice, especially a cock, and hung up votive tablets recording their names, their diseases and how they had been cured.
claims.statement_id: Semua yang sembuh mempersembahkan kurban, terutama ayam jantan, dan menggantungkan lempeng nazar yang mencatat nama, penyakit, dan cara penyembuhan mereka.
claims.quote: All who were healed offered sacrifice—especially a cock—and hung up votive tablets, on which were recorded their names, their diseases and the manner in which they had been cured.

claims.statement: Aesculapius was the legendary Greek god of medicine, son of Apollo and the nymph Coronis; Tricca in Thessaly and Epidaurus in Argolis disputed the honour of his birthplace, but an oracle declared for Epidaurus.
claims.statement_id: Aesculapius adalah dewa pengobatan Yunani legendaris, putra Apollo dan nimfa Koronis; Tricca di Thessalia dan Epidaurus di Argolis memperebutkan kehormatan sebagai tempat kelahirannya, tetapi orakel memutuskan Epidaurus.
claims.quote: the legendary Greek god of medicine, the son of Apollo and the nymph Coronis. Tricca in Thessaly and Epidaurus in Argolis disputed the honour of his birthplace, but an oracle declared in favour of Epidaurus.

claims.statement: His skill in curing disease and restoring the dead to life aroused Zeus's anger; fearing he might make all men immortal, Zeus slew him with a thunderbolt.
claims.statement_id: Keahliannya menyembuhkan penyakit dan menghidupkan orang mati membangkitkan murka Zeus, yang takut ia akan membuat semua manusia abadi, lalu membunuhnya dengan petir.
claims.quote: His skill in curing disease and restoring the dead to life aroused the anger of Zeus, who, being afraid that he might render all men immortal, slew him with a thunderbolt

claims.statement: He is commonly shown standing in a long cloak with bare breast, with a club-like staff coiled by a serpent (symbol of renovation) as his usual attribute; he is often accompanied by Telesphorus, the boy genius of healing, and his daughter Hygieia, goddess of health.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan berdiri berjubah panjang berdada terbuka dengan atribut tongkat bak gada berlilit ular (lambang pembaruan); ia sering ditemani Telesphorus, anak jenius penyembuhan, dan putrinya Hygieia, dewi kesehatan.
claims.quote: He is commonly represented standing, dressed in a long cloak, with bare breast; his usual attribute is a club-like staff with a serpent (the symbol of renovation) coiled round it. He is often accompanied by Telesphorus, the boy genius of healing, and his daughter Hygieia, the goddess of health.

claims.statement: His worship was introduced into Rome by order of the Sibylline books (293 B.C.) to avert a pestilence.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaannya dibawa ke Roma atas perintah kitab Sibylline (293 SM) untuk menolak wabah.
claims.quote: His worship was introduced into Rome by order of the Sibylline books (293 B.C.), to avert a pestilence.

claims.statement: Temples to Aesculapius were erected in many parts of Greece, near healing springs or on high mountains.
claims.statement_id: Kuil-kuil untuk Aesculapius didirikan di banyak bagian Yunani, dekat mata air penyembuh atau di gunung-gunung tinggi.
claims.quote: Temples were erected to Aesculapius in many parts of Greece, near healing springs or on high mountains.

claims.statement: The practice of sleeping (incubatio) in these sanctuaries was very common, it being supposed that the god effected cures or prescribed remedies to the sick in dreams.
claims.statement_id: Praktik tidur (incubatio) di tempat suci itu sangat umum, karena dianggap sang dewa menyembuhkan atau meresepkan obat bagi orang sakit lewat mimpi.
claims.quote: The practice of sleeping (incubatio) in these sanctuaries was very common, it being supposed that the god effected cures or prescribed remedies to the sick in dreams.

claims.statement: The motherless Asclepius was brought up by his father, who gave him the gift of healing and the secrets of medicine using plants and herbs.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius yang kehilangan ibu dibesarkan ayahnya yang memberinya karunia penyembuhan dan rahasia pengobatan dengan tumbuhan dan ramuan.
claims.quote: The motherless Asclepius was then brought up by his father who gave him the gift of healing and the secrets of medicine using plants and herbs.

claims.statement: Asclepius had many children: two sons, Machaon and Podaleirios, and four daughters, Iaso, Panacea, Aceso and Aglaia.
claims.statement_id: Asclepius punya banyak anak: dua putra, Machaon dan Podaleirios, serta empat putri, Iaso, Panacea, Aceso, dan Aglaia.
claims.quote: Asclepius had many children - two sons: Machaon and Podaleirios, and four daughters: Iaso, Panacea, Aceso, and Aglaia.

claims.statement: The father of the gods saw Asclepius and his healing art as a threat to the eternal division between humanity and the gods, especially after rumours that his healing powers were so formidable he could even raise the dead.
claims.statement_id: Ayah para dewa memandang Asclepius dan seni penyembuhannya sebagai ancaman bagi pemisahan abadi antara manusia dan dewa, terlebih setelah beredar kabar bahwa daya penyembuhannya begitu hebat hingga dapat membangkitkan orang mati.
claims.quote: This was because the father of the gods saw Asclepius and his art of healing as a threat to the eternal division between humanity and the gods, especially following rumours that Asclepius' healing powers were so formidable that he could even raise the dead

claims.statement: In some accounts Koronis abandoned her child near Epidaurus and the baby was looked after by a goat and a dog; in another Koronis was killed by Apollo for being unfaithful; in yet another the Messenian Arsinoe was his mother.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi Koronis meninggalkan bayinya dekat Epidaurus dan bayi itu dijaga seekor kambing dan anjing; versi lain menyebut Koronis dibunuh Apollo karena tidak setia; versi lain lagi menyebut Arsinoe dari Messenia sebagai ibunya.
claims.quote: In some accounts, Koronis abandoned her child near Epidaurus in shame for his illegitimacy and left the baby to be looked after by a goat and a dog. However, in a different version of the story Koronis was killed by Apollo for being unfaithful, whilst, in yet another version, the Messenian Arsinoe was the unfortunate mother of Asclepius.

claims.statement: Epidaurus was also the site of the pan-Hellenic Asklepieia festival, founded in the 5th century BCE and held every four years to celebrate theatre, sport and music in honour of Asclepius.
claims.statement_id: Epidaurus juga tempat festival Asklepieia se-Yunani yang didirikan pada abad ke-5 SM dan diadakan setiap empat tahun untuk merayakan teater, olahraga, dan musik demi menghormati Asclepius.
claims.quote: Epidaurus was also the site of the pan-Hellenic Asklepieia festival, founded in the 5th century BCE and held every four years to celebrate theatre, sport, and music in honour of Asclepius.

claims.statement: Another important sanctuary of Asclepius was in Athens, just below the Acropolis on the western slope; tradition said a priest named Telemachos brought the god there in the form of a sacred snake in 419 BCE.
claims.statement_id: Tempat suci penting lain untuk Asclepius ada di kota Athena, di lereng barat tepat di bawah Akropolis; menurut tradisi, seorang imam bernama Telemachos membawa sang dewa ke sana dalam wujud ular suci pada 419 SM.
claims.quote: Another important sanctuary in Asclepius' name was in Athens, situated just below the Acropolis on the western slope. Tradition said that a priest named Telemachos brought the god to the site in the form of a sacred snake in 419 BCE.

claims.statement: In 293 BCE the Romans were said to have taken the sacred snake from Epidaurus to the Tiber Island in order to cure a plague.
claims.statement_id: Pada 293 SM orang Romawi konon membawa ular suci dari Epidaurus ke Pulau Tiber untuk menyembuhkan wabah.
claims.quote: Finally, in 293 BCE the Romans were said to have taken the sacred snake from Epidaurus to the Tiber Island in order to cure a plague

claims.statement: The sanctuary finally closed in 426 CE when the Roman emperor Theodosius II decreed the closure of all pagan sites in Greece.
claims.statement_id: Tempat suci itu akhirnya ditutup pada 426 M ketika Kaisar Romawi Theodosius II memerintahkan penutupan semua situs pagan di Yunani.
claims.quote: The sanctuary finally closed in 426 CE when Roman emperor Theodosius II decreed the closure of all pagan sites in Greece.

claims.statement: Asclepius's descendants who continued in medicine were known as the Asclepiads; Machaon helped the wounded Menelaos in the Trojan War, but the most famous doctor of the family was undoubtedly Hippocrates.
claims.statement_id: Keturunan Asclepius yang melanjutkan seni pengobatan disebut Asclepiad; Machaon membantu Menelaos yang terluka dalam Perang Troya, tetapi dokter paling terkenal di keluarga itu tak diragukan lagi Hippocrates.
claims.quote: The descendants of Asclepius, who continued in the art of medicine and healing, were known as the Asclepiads. Machaon, for example, helped Menelaos when he was wounded in the Trojan War, but the most famous doctor of the family was undoubtedly Hippocrates.

claims.statement: He is sometimes accompanied by Hygeia and occasionally has a dog at his feet, as these animals were sacred at some of his sanctuaries.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang ditemani Hygeia dan sesekali ada anjing di kakinya, karena hewan-hewan itu dianggap suci di beberapa tempat sucinya.
claims.quote: He is sometimes accompanied by Hygeia and occasionally has a dog at his feet, as these animals were sacred at some of the god's sanctuaries.

claims.statement: Apollo protested against his son's treatment but was himself punished by Zeus for impiety and made to serve Admetos, king of Thessaly, for one year.
claims.statement_id: Apollo memprotes perlakuan terhadap putranya tetapi dihukum Zeus karena ketidaksalehan dan dipaksa melayani Admetos, raja Thessalia, selama satu tahun.
claims.quote: Apollo protested against his son's treatment but was himself punished by Zeus for impiety and made to serve Admetos, the king of Thessaly, for one year.

claims.statement: Thankful patients often left votive offerings at the site, sometimes depicting the body part that had been cured.
claims.statement_id: Pasien yang bersyukur sering meninggalkan persembahan nazar di tempat itu, kadang menggambarkan bagian tubuh yang sembuh.
claims.quote: Thankful patients often left votive offerings at the site, sometimes depicting the body part which had been cured.

claims.statement: Snakes were associated with Asclepius and symbolised regeneration, as they were thought to live both below and above ground, and were connected to prophetic powers as they knew the hidden secrets below ground.
claims.statement_id: Ular dikaitkan dengan Asclepius dan melambangkan regenerasi karena dianggap hidup di bawah dan di atas tanah, dan juga dikaitkan dengan daya ramal karena mengetahui rahasia tersembunyi di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: These were associated with Asclepius and symbolised regeneration, as snakes were thought to live both below and above ground and were also connected to prophetic powers as they knew the hidden secrets below ground.

claims.statement: In some traditions he was married to Hygeia, also a goddess of health; in another version she was his daughter and Asclepius married Epione.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa tradisi ia menikah dengan Hygeia, juga dewi kesehatan; dalam versi lain Hygeia adalah putrinya dan Asclepius menikahi Epione.
claims.quote: In some traditions he was married to Hygeia, also a goddess of health; in another version she was his daughter and Asclepius married Epione.

claims.statement: The cult of Asclepius was also transferred to Pergamon sometime in the 4th century BCE, possibly by a healed patient at Epidaurus named Archias.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Asclepius juga dipindahkan ke Pergamon pada suatu waktu di abad ke-4 SM, mungkin oleh pasien sembuh di Epidaurus bernama Archias.
claims.quote: The cult of Asclepius was also transferred to Pergamon sometime in the 4th century BCE, possibly by a healed patient at Epidaurus named Archias.

claims.statement: The serpent, Aesculapius's perpetual symbol, has given rise to the opinion that his worship was derived from Egypt and that he was identical with the serpent Cnuph worshipped in Egypt or the Phoenician Esmun.
claims.statement_id: Ular, lambang abadi Aesculapius, melahirkan pendapat bahwa pemujaannya berasal dari Mesir dan bahwa Aesculapius identik dengan ular Cnuph yang dipuja di Mesir atau dengan Esmun dari Fenisia.
claims.quote: The serpent, the perpetual symbol of Aesculapius, has given rise to the opinion, that the worship was derived from Egypt, and that Aesculapius was identical with the serpent Cnuph worshipped in Egypt, or with the Phoenician Esmun.

claims.statement: According to others, the cause was that Pluto had complained that Aesculapius diminished the number of the dead too much.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian lain, penyebabnya adalah Pluto mengeluh bahwa Aesculapius terlalu banyak mengurangi jumlah orang mati.
claims.quote: or, according to others, because Pluto had complained of Aesculapius diminishing the number of the dead too much.

claims.statement: Asklepios' apotheosis into godhood occurred at the same time; he was sometimes identified with Homer's Paion (Paeon), the physician of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Apoteosis Asklepios menjadi dewa terjadi pada saat yang sama; ia kadang diidentifikasi dengan Paion (Paeon) dalam Homeros, tabib para dewa.
claims.quote: Asklepios' apotheosis into godhood occurred at the same time. He was sometimes identified with Homer's Paion (Paeon), the physician of the gods.

claims.statement: Here was the god's most famous shrine, and games were celebrated in his honour every five years, accompanied by solemn processions.
claims.statement_id: Di sinilah tempat suci sang dewa yang paling terkenal, dan pertandingan diadakan untuk menghormatinya setiap lima tahun disertai prosesi khidmat.
claims.quote: Here was the god’s most famous shrine, and games were celebrated in his honour every five years, accompanied by solemn processions.

claims.statement: The sanctuary at Epidaurus was known as the Asklepieion because he was believed to have been born on the nearby Mt. Titthion.
claims.statement_id: Epidaurus dikenal sebagai Asklepieion karena ia dipercaya lahir di Gunung Titthion di dekatnya.
claims.quote: known as the Asklepieion, because he was believed to have been born on the nearby Mt. Titthion.
